docs.heaps.component: On a desk, cards lie on cards and chips on chips. A heap is not a declared container — it is an emergent island of touching pieces.

To a player, two cards a hair apart on a felt are touching. Requiring an exact mathematical intersection of zero would feel brittle and broken. `TOUCH_SLACK = 0.04` units provides the forgiveness needed for natural heap formation.
Only pieces of matching kind heap together: cards join cards, chips join chips of their own denomination, and dice never heap (each die is individual).
What may lie in one heap is governed by four questions asked at four separate times:
1. **`joins(a, b)`**: May these two pieces ever form a heap? (Semantic affinity, no geometry).
2. **`meets(a, b, oa, ob)`**: Are their outlines close enough? (Pure geometry with `TOUCH_SLACK` or overlap share).
3. **`admits(group)`**: Which pieces of the found island does the heap keep? (Evaluated bottom-first after islands are found, allowing rules based on top coverage).
4. **`seats(group, gripW)`**: Where each piece stands when the heap is lifted by its handle.

A piece currently in the air or being carried by a hand (`aloft(id)`) cannot be in any heap: it left the heap the moment it was picked up. Including it would cause handles to pull flying cards out of the air.
- `heapsOf` computes connected components via union-find (`islands`). Lone pieces are dropped: a single card is not a heap, and a handle under it would be a dead control.
- `heapBox` calculates the common perimeter and bottom coordinate where the stack handle will stand.
docs.heaps.heaps: Interactive demonstration of `heaps.ts`. Cards and chips start separated. Push two cards or two chips together: as soon as their outlines meet within `TOUCH_SLACK = 0.04`, they join into a heap and a handle appears beneath them.
